fundamentals_narrative: Apcotex is India's only domestic producer of NBR (acrylonitrile butadiene rubber), plus nitrile/SBR latex for paper, carpet and construction -- a genuine domestic niche monopoly. But it is a commodity polymer whose earnings track the global NBR/latex spread cycle: PAT halved from Rs 108 Cr (FY23) to Rs 54 Cr in FY24 and FY25 as spreads collapsed, then recovered to Rs 101 Cr in FY26. Q1 FY27 was a record (revenue Rs 526 Cr +40%, EBITDA margin 22.3% vs 10.3%, PAT Rs 79 Cr +311%), but both management and the VP community flag it as flattered: ~2% of EBITDA was one-off inventory gains, the improvement was price-realisation-led (domestic volumes +10% but export volumes -10-12% on West Asia logistics), and management states the 22.3% margin is 'not a normalized level' against a 15-16% through-cycle target. The forward levers are real but qualified: a Rs 220 Cr NBR + synthetic-latex expansion (adds ~Rs 600 Cr topline, on stream Q1 FY28) is on track and largely self-funded from a net-cash balance sheet, and the DGTR recommended a 5-year anti-dumping duty on NBR imports in Sept 2025 -- but the Finance Ministry has still not notified it, and the new capacity will not carry ADD protection. Management deferred its Stage 2 NBR expansion by 3-4 months, explicitly citing new capacity in Malaysia and 'the China factor' -- i.e. the supply side is adding globally. At ~5x book and ~24x normalised earnings for a cyclical polymer with mid-teens through-cycle returns, the valuation already prices a sustained up-cycle.
